text: You may remember, let me just temporarily, ah, go ahead a bit. You may remember from high school, the law according to which electromagnetic signals propagate in the simplest and ideal case, that is free space, where there are no obstacles, there is just a transmitter and a receiver. I'm sure in high school you studied that this formula, that says that the power of the received signal, of course depends on the power with which the signal is transmitted, and then it depends on the type of antenna that we are using, and then it depends on the distance, right? So it gets attenuated with the square of the distance. That means that if transmitter and receiver are very close to each other, then the receiver will get a high power signal, but if the receiver is far away, it will get a much weaker signal, right? So r is the distance between transmitter and receiver, and let me show you this version essentially of of the formula of the attenuation that is experienced by a signal, where even more clearly we see the dependency of the attenuation L on the distance between transmitter and receiver. Okay, this in detail, the attenuation increases with the square of the distance, but also it increases.
